Press Release:


Fall of Riah Phiyega
Police commissioner Riah Phiyega may soon be axed if a commission of inquiry finds her unfit to hold office. But the Marikana report is not the first to question the competence of the National Police Commissioner. She has, since the start of her 3-year tenure, faced massive criticism from politicians and the public who allege she was never up to the job. Is this the consequence of an inexperienced political appointee heading up the SAPS? Carte Blanche investigates.


Script:


FINAL VERSION SCRIPT
SCRIPT: CARTE BLANCHE PHIYEGA
SIAN CLARK
TX: JULY 5th
VOICEOVER: DEREK WATTS – July 3rd.

UP SOUND: RIAH PHIYEGA: THIS RESPONSIBILITY I ACCEPT WITH THE GREATEST HUMILITY JUST BECAUSE OF IT’S SHEER SIZE, ITS SCOPE AND WHAT IT MEANS FOR THIS NATION.

64 days later the Marikana Massacre shocked the country …..

44 people died -including 34 striking miners who had staged a sit-in on this koppie just outside the Lonmon Mine in the North West Province.

Pan Overlay of newspapers see the headlines
Last week the release of the 650 page Marikana Report saw one name dominate the headlines.
Soundbite:
Gareth Newham : National Police commissioner Riah Phiyega WAS FULLY AWARE about the plan was about … she disregarded any warnings of bloodshed and then she led a cover up.

Soundbite:
ADAM HABIB
02.18 IT’S ANOTHER EXAMPLE OF BAD APPOINTMENTS THAT HAVE COME TO HAUNT US 02.23

Derek link three years:
Three years after the Marikana massacre there are few signs of the bloodshed and the lives being lost yet the repercussions are still being felt especially when it comes to our police commissioner

V/O: Following the recent Marikana Report’s recommendations, President Zuma requested Riah Phiyega’s fitness to hold office be investigated.

UP SOUND: JACOB ZUMA THERE MUST BE AN INQUIRY INTO THE FITNESS TO HOLD OFFICE OF THE NATIONAL POLICE COMMISIONER.
Professor
ADAM 00.00.10
clip: 002Q1: The Commission’s report does asks the question whether the police commissioner IS it for office .. and it does that so categorically .. but that does not mean that President Jacob zuma get’s off stock free .. who appointed her in first place …


Political Scientist Adam Habib says many people warned the Presidency that Riah Phiyega was a bad choice for the top job of National Police Commisionner.


ADAM
00.00.35
when she was appointed he was warned … there were many responses that says she does not have operational expertise … you bringing somebody from outside the police services but what you need is someone with experience in this regard ..00.00.54

V/O
Many have argued that after the controversies surrounding previous Police Commissioners Jackie Selebi and Bheki Cele that filling this key position should be taken far more seriously.

In June 2012 Polokwane born Mangwashi Victoria Phiyega became the first woman to hold the post of National Police Commissioner. Two months later she described the Police reaction to the Marikana protests as “the best of responsible policing”.

FROM EWN UP SOUND: RIAH PHIYEGA
AS A LEADER I HAD TO COME IN AND actually say let’s be strong, let’s move on… Remember all we can do is tell how how we policed, all we can do is tell how we experienced the event and all we can do is tell the truth as we know it.


ADAM 01.48 I think she was appointed because very powerful people felt that she can be controlled, she was a loyal cadre, and THAT’S THE PROBLEM nothing stood out, that suggested that she would be an independent person own right, with the kind of managerial experience that would allow us to address the challenges in the police services. 02.19

UPSOUND: Gareth: The first statement that the police commissioner released to the people of South Africa was misleading she tried to mislead all of us and then she tried to mislead a Judicial commission of Inquiry by being untruthful … and overseeing the construction of false and misleading evidence.

GARETH TITLE CHECK FOR VO: The Institute for Security Studies’ Gareth Newham questions whether Riah Phiyega allowed political issues to cloud her decision making at the time of the Marikana protests.

GARETH UPSOUND:
Head of the Governance, Crime & Justice Division ISS 00.16.27 we have highly skilled, highly qualified expert police officers … but they are often not appointed to key positions because they are politically neutral. They will not take orders from Politian’s they believe to be incorrect. they wll only follow the laws and regulations and that is our single biggest challenge. 00.16.42


Derek link OUTSIDE WITS 0260Y7
She has a string of degrees and held a number of top corporate positions before being named as the Police Commissioner. She is not new to controversy in fact it seems to have dogged her career.


Portnet footage
Transnet logo and port footage
VO
Trained as a Social Worker Riah Phiyega became Group executive at Transnet, largely responsible for restructuring Portnet. She didn’t see out her contract but opted for a termination package with media reports at the time claiming the company was undertaking a purge of non-performing executives.

She became Head of the National Development Agency and then moved to Absa for five years. She left as Group Executive, reportedly to pursue interests outside the group.
Date this as Carte Blanche June 2012 General Phiyega: "I've learnt from business. I have the opportunity to take from business to the public sector. Those skills are versatile; an organisation is an organisation. Whether you run a family, whether you run a church, whether you run ABSA, you have to nuance those skills and just make sure your organisation succeeds."

UPSOUND GARETH:
00.15.10 your degrees and qualifications or your previous management in private sector or banking are never going to be able to help you … so you have to have somebody who understands policing.’

Riah smiling Vo She caught the President’s eye when she was appointed as chairwoman of the Presidential state-owned Enterprise Review Committee.
VO: As National Police Commissioner she has certainly left her mark.


VO: She withdrew her appointment of Bethuel Zuma as new Gauteng provincial commissioner just hours after appointing him when she allegedly discovered his pending criminal charges.

A month later she placed the new acting crime intelligence head Chris Ngcobo on special leave, after it emerged that there were "discrepancies" in his qualifications.

And she was recently accused of allagedly tipping off Western Cape police commissioner Arno Lamoer about a potential probe by crime intelligence.

UP SOUND: PROFESSOR MALULEKE
02.20 I think her position is untenable … she is unlikely to command much respect from the people that she leads

Vo: Speaking to us from London Political analyst Professor Tinyiko Maluleke questioned Phiyega’s legacy thus far.
UP SOUND: PROFESSOR MALULEKE
“I think she is unlikely to inspire a lot of confidence from the ministry of police and presidents and, I think the public is going to be very skeptical about her integrity going forward.”

VO:
Phiyega’s integrity was questioned in 2014 when she wore various high ranking police medals at the National Police Remembrance Day including the 10-year commemoration medal - for service in the first 10 years of democracy. What has happened to the police force under her watch?

Gareth: 00.17.39 For most of the past 10 years most of the police leaving the police services on an annual basis have been around 2000 or 300 it’s gone up to 7000 last year … ..
We have seen a dramatic surge in serious organized violent crime since 2011 2012 and we have seen 18 000 more armed attack than there were two years previously when Phiyega took over and that was her legacy for the last two years … 00.19.07.

UP SOUND: PHIYEGA
My rank my title have very little to do with the morale of the police. what has got to do with the morale is whether as a leader I am able to give that inspirational guidance … whether I am able to hold a very bright torch
DEREK LINK 0261LF
THERE HAVE BEEN CALLS FOR HER TO RESIGN, FIRED. EXPERTS SAY SHE WONT’ LEAVE WITHOUT A FIGHT AND COULD TAKE OTHERS DOWN WITH HER.


PROFESSOR MALULEKE: the honourable thing is for her to resign and I think that is the suggestion that is coming from the president and I am afraid I see another golden handshake coming.
Timelapse of the cross VO:
The President has invited General Phiyega to respond to the inquiry by no later than the 31st of July. No public pronouncements about the Marikana report, its findings and recommendations will be made by the Police until then.

ENDS ENDS








PROMO ONE 15 SECONDS:
National Police Commissioner Riah Phiyega’s position is under scrutiny following the outcome of the Marikana report. But should she have been appointed to begin with.
ADAM HABIB It’s another example of bad appointments that have come to haunt us.


PROMO TWO:
Following the Marikana report the National Police Commissioner Riah Phiyega may be axed if a new Commission of Inquiry finds her unfit for office.
GARETH NEWHAM “ She disregarded any warnings of bloodshed and then she led a cover up”


PROMO 10 SECONDS:
Will the axe of the Marikana report fall onto National Police Commissioner RIAH PHIYEGA.
ADAM 01.48 “very powerful people felt that she can be controlled.”
